issues.title: Partition count(DISTINCT) radix table on the group-key hash only
issues.hypothesis: Measured this round on a temp table t holding q16's join output (1.18M rows, 27.8k groups): count(DISTINCT x) GROUP BY G takes 102-145 ms wall, SELECT DISTINCT G,x takes 65 ms, and GROUP BY G count(*) takes 30 ms. So after the distinct table is built, about 40 ms of wall goes to re-aggregating the 1.18M distinct tuples into the main table (E0002/E0004 timers: main-HT sink ~180 ms CPU plus main finalize ~30 ms CPU). The distinct radix table partitions on hash(G,x), so every distinct partition holds tuples of every group. Each of the 8 distinct-finalize tasks (AggregateDistinctGrouping, physical_hash_aggregate.cpp:648) therefore feeds all 28k groups into its local main HT. That HT has capacity 32768 and a resize threshold of 21845, so it abandons repeatedly, and the main finalize then combines about 8x or more duplicate group rows. If the radix bits of the distinct table's stored hash come from hash(G) alone, each distinct partition holds complete groups. Then each task's main local HT only sees ~28k*(partitions handled)/(total partitions) groups: it stays small and cache-resident, never abandons, and the main combine/finalize handles ~1x the groups. Salt (top 16 bits) and slot bits (low bits) keep coming from the full hash(G,x), so probe quality in the distinct HT is unchanged.
issues.plan: 1) GroupedAggregateHashTable (src/execution/aggregate_hashtable.cpp + header): add an optional member `idx_t partition_key_count = 0` (0 = off) with a setter. Add a private helper `HashGroups(DataChunk &groups, Vector &hashes)`. It calls groups.Hash(hashes). When partition_key_count > 0 it also hashes only the first partition_key_count columns into a scratch HASH vector (DataChunk::Hash with a column subset, or VectorOperations::Hash/CombineHash over those columns in the same order DataChunk::Hash uses, so the values equal what the main table computes for G). It then splices: h = (h_full & ~RadixPartitioning::Mask(RadixPartitioning::MAX_RADIX_BITS)) | (h_G & Mask(MAX_RADIX_BITS)), i.e. bits [36,48) come from G. Use the helper at every place this HT hashes raw groups: AddChunk(groups,payload,filter) ~line 528, the dictionary/constant paths in TryAddCompressedGroups (~lines 428 and 480; simplest is to skip TryAddCompressedGroups when the option is on), and FindOrCreateGroups(groups, addresses, new_groups) ~line 830. Combine, Repartition and finalize reuse the stored hash column, so they stay consistent. 2) RadixPartitionedHashTable (src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp): add a field set at construction and pass it to the HT in CreateHT (line 71). 3) DistinctAggregateData constructor (src/execution/operator/aggregate/distinct_aggregate_data.cpp:75-115): when group_expressions is non-null and groups is non-empty, set partition_key_count = groups.size() on the radix table. grouping_set is an ordered set with the group indices (< group_by_size) first, so the first groups.size() HT columns are exactly G in the same order as the main table's grouping set. Optional gate: skip when the aggregate's estimated_cardinality is small (e.g. < 4096 estimated groups), where few groups would skew the distinct partitions. Check q16's estimate with EXPLAIN before choosing the threshold, so q16 is not gated off. 4) Verify: results of q16 plus count(DISTINCT) with GROUPING SETS/ROLLUP, multiple distinct aggregates on different columns, distinct with FILTER, a NULL group key, and spilling (memory_limit 100MB). Bench q16. If the gain is small, check that the main local HT really stops abandoning, e.g. with a temporary counter.
issues.expected_gain: q16: 5-12%. It removes most of the ~210 ms CPU in the main re-sink and finalize (about 15-25 ms wall of ~180).
issues.generality: Any grouped DISTINCT aggregate (count/sum/avg DISTINCT ... GROUP BY) with many groups, such as TPC-H q16 and the 'distinct users per key' pattern. It could get slower when there are very few groups and many distinct values (e.g. GROUP BY a boolean): the distinct partitions become skewed and finalize parallelism drops. The estimated-cardinality gate limits that case. Ungrouped DISTINCT is untouched.
issues.risk: Medium-low. Correctness only needs every insert into the distinct HT to use the same hash function. The risk is missing a hash site, e.g. the dictionary fast path or FindOrCreateGroups overloads, which would produce duplicate distinct tuples and wrong counts. Needs careful audit plus tests with dictionary-encoded group columns. The HLL in FindOrCreateGroupsInternal sees a slightly less random hash, which has negligible effect on adaptivity.

dispatch: Partition count(DISTINCT) radix table on the group-key hash only
output.memory:
## Memory (gen1 round5)

### Workload
- Only template q16: partsupp JOIN part (filtered: brand<>, type NOT LIKE prefix, size IN 8 consts) + NOT IN (supplier LIKE) mark join, GROUP BY brand,type,size count(DISTINCT suppkey). ~27.8k groups, ~1.18M rows into the agg. Bench ~155-200 ms; the machine is very noisy and the first run in a dbe-tool sql call is cold (always discard it).
- Wall split (warm): join-only query 62 ms; full q16 ~155-180 ms.

### R5 measurements (temp table t = q16 join output, packed chunks, warm)
- count(DISTINCT x) GROUP BY G: 102-145 ms wall (HASH_GROUP_BY 0.41-0.55 s CPU)
- SELECT DISTINCT G,x: 65 ms
- GROUP BY G count(*): 30 ms
- So distinct build ~65 ms, plus re-aggregating into the main table ~40 ms.
- Sparse chunks (~290 rows, from t2 = t x range(7) WHERE k=0): agg CPU 0.46-0.61 vs 0.41-0.55. Chunk compaction is only ~10% of agg CPU and noisy, so it is a weak lever. CACHE_THRESHOLD = 64 (physical_operator.hpp:270) is why 300-row join outputs pass uncompacted.
- R5 dispatched: partition the distinct radix table on hash(G) bits only (bits [36,48) spliced from the G hash; salt and slot bits stay from the full hash). Each finalize task's main HT then sees only its partitions' groups: no abandon thrash, ~1x combine.
- If R5 works, follow-up: with aligned partitions the main table could be bypassed entirely (count per G directly while scanning each distinct partition).

### KEY FINDING R4: the non-inlined VARCHAR key (p_type, 25 chars) costs the aggregate
- DISTINCT on the 4 keys: 46-59 ms (p_type) vs 35 (hash) vs 29 (fixed-width).
- CompressedMaterialization packs strings up to 16 bytes only; p_type is too long.
- TryAddDictionaryGroups (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:359) only works for a single dictionary group column.

### Exhausted / no-gain directions (do not repeat)
- E0001 early HT grow: ~3%. E0002 and E0004 (the same fix: unpartitioned staging only for AllConstant layouts): -0.6% / -1.3% wall, despite ~110 ms CPU less. E0003 early SkipLookups: ≤3%. Sink-side probe/staging tweaks are exhausted.
- Manual 2-level rewrite of count(DISTINCT): same speed.
- Lesson: CPU savings in the distinct sink of ~100 ms don't show in wall time (the sink overlaps the join pipeline). Target the finalize-side phases, which are serial after the pipeline: distinct finalize, main re-sink, main finalize.

### Codebase facts
- Radix aggregate HT (src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp): with more than 2 threads the sink capacity is 32768 (resize threshold 21845). Abandon() when full. DecideAdaptation runs at 1M rows per thread. MAXIMUM_FINAL_SINK_RADIX_BITS = 8. CreateHT is at line 71.
- Hash bit layout: salt = top 16 bits. Radix bits = [48-r, 48) with r ≤ RadixPartitioning::MAX_RADIX_BITS = 12 (radix_partitioning.hpp:45-52). Slot = low bits.
- Hash sites in GroupedAggregateHashTable: AddChunk ~528, dictionary paths ~428/480, FindOrCreateGroups ~830. Combine and finalize reuse the stored hash column.
- Distinct tables are built in DistinctAggregateData ctor (distinct_aggregate_data.cpp:75). grouping_set is an ordered set: group indices first, then the distinct children.
- AggregateDistinctGrouping (physical_hash_aggregate.cpp:648-754) GetData's the distinct radix table and Sinks into the main table_data with a per-task local sink state, then Combine. CanSkipRegularSink skips the main sink in the pipeline when all aggregates are distinct.
- The per-partition finalize is RadixHTLocalSourceState::Finalize (~line 853): new HT + Combine.
- TupleDataAllocator::RecomputeHeapPointers (tuple_data_allocator.cpp:533).
- Perfect HJ: CanDoPerfectHashJoin (perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:66), MAX_BUILD_SIZE = 1048576. CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:761) returns false for a perfect HT, so a perfect HJ would lose the partsupp BF (8M rows down to 1.24M).
- InClauseRewriter: IN lists with >= 6 constants become a MARK join.
- dbe-tool: several statements in one `sql` call work (CREATE TEMP TABLE then EXPLAIN ANALYZE x2), and piping into grep is allowed. Wrapping in count(*) can drop the distinct aggregate; use max(col).

### Backlog ideas (ranked)
1. (dispatched R5) G-only radix bits for the distinct table.
2. Bypass the main table after #1 (direct per-partition counting).
3. Dictionary-ID substitution for long-string group keys (large).
4. Perfect HJ for sparse ranges (BF caveat; doubtful).
5. IN-list filter in the scan instead of the mark join (2-4%).
6. Chunk compaction (raise CACHE_THRESHOLD): ≤5%, weak.

### Prior-run notes (other workloads, see MEMORY index): perfect HJ / large perfect HA gave ~20% on q13.
